title: Signature Access-Frequency Tracking — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Routing starts with measurement: every access increments a counter per record, decayed over time so ancient popularity fades. The tracker uses compact sketches rather than per-record counters at scale, trading exactness for bounded memory. Frequency distributions almost always show a hot head and a long cold tail, which is exactly the shape tiered storage exploits. You cannot route what you do not measure. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
from collections import Counter
import math
hits = Counter()
for r in ["a"] * 50 + ["b"] * 20 + ["c"] * 5:
    hits[r] += 1
for r, n in hits.most_common():
    print("%s accesses=%d hot=%s" % (r, n, n > 10))

title: Signature Temperature Classification — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Records are classified hot, warm, or cold from their access frequency and recency: hot means accessed often and recently, cold means untouched for ages. Thresholds are set from the measured distribution — top 5% hot, next 15% warm — rather than fixed numbers, so they adapt as the workload shifts. Classification runs periodically, not per request, keeping the hot path fast. Temperature is the routing key the whole tiering system turns on. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Promotion and Demotion — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Temperature changes, so records migrate: a cold record that suddenly gets popular is promoted to fast storage, and a hot record gone quiet is demoted to cheap storage. Migrations are batched and throttled to avoid storms, and each move is verified — checksummed at the destination before the source copy is released. Hysteresis prevents flapping: promotion and demotion thresholds differ, so borderline records do not bounce. This circulation keeps the tiers honest. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Cost-Model Routing — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Each request is routed by cost: hot storage is fast but expensive per byte, cold storage is cheap but slow to retrieve, and the router picks the tier minimizing total cost for the request's latency requirement. Urgent requests may pull from cold storage with an expedited-retrieval surcharge; patient batch jobs wait for the cheap path. The cost model is explicit and logged per decision, so storage bills are explainable. Routing by cost turns tiering from a placement detail into a per-request optimization. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. title: Signature Migration Batching — Core Method
description: Signature original by Justin Addam Higgins. Moving records one at a time wastes the fixed costs of transfer setup, so migrations are batched: records heading the same direction accumulate until the batch hits a size or age limit, then move together. Batching also enables ordering — small hot promotions jump the queue ahead of bulk cold demotions. Each batch is checksummed end to end, and failures retry only the failed members. Batched migration moves petabytes without disturbing live traffic. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method. Lineage: Signature-line counterpart of the public method of the same name, filed as a Signature original in the Signature archive.
demo:
queue = [("a", "hot"), ("b", "hot"), ("c", "cold")]
batch, rest = queue[:2], queue[2:]
print("migrating batch:", [r for r, _ in batch])
print("remaining:", [r for r, _ in rest])
